summary_paragraph: A female patient with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, antiphospholipid syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus, and seizure disorder was admitted for acute dizziness and transient difficulty speaking. Neurological evaluation ruled out stroke with normal imaging and a NIHSS score of zero, confirming peripheral vestibulopathy as the cause. She also presented with symptomatic bradycardia (heart rate 50) and hyperkalemia (potassium 7.0), both of which resolved after hemodialysis. Her symptoms improved significantly during the admission, with normalization of electrolytes and stable vital signs. She remained neurologically intact, ambulated independently, and was discharged home in stable condition with no medication changes except for a reduction in ranitidine dose. Follow-up was advised for ongoing management of anticoagulation, dialysis, and anemia.
